title: A Safehouse for the Protocol
premise: Vesper Thornbury, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Group — an embassy that exists on no map — answers a burner phone that should have been destroyed years ago and hears the voice of her presumed-dead mentor, Elias Vance, who warns that an attack disguised as an industrial accident will hit Frankfurt before markets open. Ordered by Meridian to stand down because the truth implicates their own founders, Vesper must choose between the institution that gave her a name and a purpose, and the loyalty she owes to a man who taught her every lie she knows. As she races through Vienna's back channels with a defector analyst who forces her to question everything, she discovers the 'accident' is a cover for Meridian laundering its own history. In the end, Vesper burns her polished lie to expose the protocol, saves Frankfurt at the cost of her old life, and finally stops running — choosing belonging over duty.
about_author: Elodie Fairweather is the pen name of a former diplomatic translator who spent a decade in European capitals watching what official histories leave out. She writes thrillers about people who keep secrets for a living and pay for them in love.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A routine extraction in Vienna establishes her world: forged papers, a packed bag by the door, a life built to be abandoned in ninety seconds. When her handler orders her to destroy an old evidence cache, she hesitates — and keeps one burner phone instead. Emotional beat: the quiet unease of a woman whose competence has replaced her identity.

chapters.title: A Voice from the Burner
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The kept phone rings at 3 a.m.: Elias Vance, dead for six years, speaking in the coded cadence they invented together. He gives her a timestamp — Frankfurt, before market open — and a warning that Meridian is inside the plot. Emotional beat: vertigo; grief and hope colliding as the past refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: Stand Down
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, with a brief handler-side interlude. Meridian orders her to ignore the call and fly home; her refusal is noted in a file she isn't meant to see. She begins pulling threads off-book, using favors she can never repay. Emotional beat: the first conscious betrayal — thrilling and terrifying, like stepping off a ledge.

chapters.title: The Analyst Who Defected Wrong
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Hunting the source of the attack's logistics, she finds Nadia Reiss, a disgraced financial-crimes analyst hiding in a Prague safehouse, holding transaction records that point at Meridian's own founding families. Distrust sparks into reluctant alliance. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's craftsmanship.

chapters.title: What the Protocol Buried
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Through intercepted ledgers, we learn the 'protocol' is decades of disguised payments — and the Frankfurt attack is designed to erase the last physical proof. Nadia reveals she was burned by the same network that killed Elias. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into resolve; belonging found in shared damage.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A meet with Elias's intermediary goes wrong — the intermediary is killed by someone using Meridian tradecraft, and Vesper realizes the voice on the phone may be bait. She confronts the possibility that Elias is alive but compromised. Emotional beat: love against duty sharpening into suspicion; trust becomes a calculated risk.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Before Open
chapters.summary: Vesper and Nadia's alternating POV. With hours left, they trace the attack to a data-center fire staged as electrical failure, timed to vaporize the ledger archive during a market holiday lull. Meridian locks down their travel; they go dark, moving through freight corridors. Emotional beat: the ticking clock compresses fear into clarity.

chapters.title: The Man Who Taught Her to Lie
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She finds Elias alive in a Meridian black site outside the city — kept as leverage, his voice used to lure dissenters. He begs her to walk away; she chooses instead to use his access codes, the last gift of her teacher, against the institution. Emotional beat: heartbreak transmuted into weaponized loyalty.

chapters.title: Accident, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Vesper and Nadia's POV, intercut. Inside the data center, they trigger the fire suppression early and mirror the ledger to journalists and regulators before Meridian's cleaners arrive. Vesper faces the operation's architect — her own handler — and chooses exposure over silence, broadcasting the protocol live. Emotional beat: climax; duty inverted, truth chosen at gunpoint.

chapters.title: A Safehouse of Her Own
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, weeks later. Meridian is fracturing under investigation; Elias, freed but broken, disappears to answer for his compromises. Vesper unpacks the go-bag for the first time in years, keeping only the burner — now a line to Nadia. Emotional beat: resolution; the woman built to vanish finally stays, having traded a polished lie for an unpolished home.
